body.statement: For every \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0\le r<1\), the map \(x\mapsto q_{\beta}(r,x)\) is convex on \(\mathbb R\). Moreover, for every \(c_0,c_1\in\mathbb R\) and \(0<t<1\), \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\) holds if and only if \(r=0\) or \(c_0=c_1\).
body.justification: Convexity supplies the global single-crossing reduction, with exact symbolic equality strata.
body.gap: The cited Ehrhard equality theorem does not itself state the selected-score quantile result.
body.consumer: A compact positive alternative set enters only through least coordinates.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\gamma_2\) be standard Gaussian measure on \(\mathbb R^2\), and define
\[
\mathcal O(c,z)=[c,\infty)\times[z,\infty),
\qquad
\mathcal T(c,z)=Q^{-1}\{Q(c)Q(z)\}.
\]
Minkowski interpolation of two such orthants is the orthant having the interpolated thresholds.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}ehrhard\mbox{-}borell\mbox{-}convex\mbox{-}equality}\), and using \(Q^{-1}(u)=-\Phi^{-1}(u)\), yields
\[
\mathcal T((1-t)c_0+tc_1,(1-t)z_0+tz_1)
\le(1-t)\mathcal T(c_0,z_0)+t\mathcal T(c_1,z_1).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal T\) is jointly convex.  If \(Z\) is standard normal, then \(Q(Z)\) is uniform on \((0,1)\), and for \(y>c\),
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal T(c,Z)>y\}=\frac{Q(y)}{Q(c)}.
\]
Therefore \(\mathcal T(c,Z)\) has the distribution of a standard normal conditional on exceeding \(c\).

Put \(v=\sqrt{1-r^2}>0\), \(W(c,z,e)=r\mathcal T(c,z)+ve\), and
\[
\mathcal A(c,q)=\{(z,e):W(c,z,e)\le q\}.
\]
For \(r\ge0\), \(W\) is convex, and hence
\[
(1-t)\mathcal A(c_0,q_0)+t\mathcal A(c_1,q_1)
\subseteq
\mathcal A((1-t)c_0+tc_1,(1-t)q_0+tq_1).
\]
Take \(q_i=q_\beta(r,c_i)\).  The two sets on the left each have Gaussian measure \(1-\beta\).  Ehrhard--Borell and the inclusion imply that the set on the right has measure at least \(1-\beta\).  Since the independent term \(vE\) supplies a positive continuous density, the quantile is unique, and
\[
q_\beta(r,(1-t)c_0+tc_1)
\le(1-t)q_\beta(r,c_0)+tq_\beta(r,c_1).
\]
This proves convexity.

If \(r=0\), this quantile is the constant \(\Phi^{-1}(1-\beta)\); if \(c_0=c_1\), chord equality is immediate.  Conversely, suppose \(r>0\), \(c_0\ne c_1\), and chord equality holds.  Equality must then hold in the preceding Gaussian-measure comparison.  The equality clause of the cited lemma says that \(\mathcal A(c_0,q_0)\) and \(\mathcal A(c_1,q_1)\) are parallel half-spaces or equal modulo Gaussian null sets.  They are not half-spaces: their boundaries are the nonaffine graphs
\[
e=\{q-r\mathcal T(c,z)\}/v,
\]
because \(\mathcal T(c,z)\to c\) as \(z\to-\infty\) and \(\mathcal T(c,z)\to\infty\) as \(z\to\infty\).  Equality modulo null sets of these closed convex sets implies equality, so the two boundary graphs would make \(\mathcal T(c_0,z)-\mathcal T(c_1,z)\) constant.  Its limit at \(-\infty\) is \(c_0-c_1\).  If this constant were nonzero, the elementary Mills inequalities
\[
\frac{\phi(x)}{x+x^{-1}}<Q(x)<\frac{\phi(x)}x\qquad(x>0)
\]
would make \(Q(\mathcal T(c_0,z))/Q(\mathcal T(c_1,z))\) tend to zero or infinity as \(z\to\infty\), whereas its defining identity makes that ratio equal to \(Q(c_0)/Q(c_1)\).  Hence the constant is zero, which forces \(c_0=c_1\), a contradiction.  These are exactly the asserted equality strata.
